sample_size.location: abstract, first sentence; total_n derived from reported group counts 50 + 99 = 149

cases.excerpt: This case-control study aimed to assess the association of dairy-derived digestion-resistant bioactive peptides (BPs) with the risk of prostate cancer (PCa) in a cohort of 50 men with PCa and 99 controls.

effect_size.excerpt: High intake of total digestion-resistant BPs, low molecular weight peptides, high molecular weight peptides, phosphorylated residues, disulfide bonds, and antioxidant peptides was not significantly associated with the risk of PCa in the adjusted models (P>0.05), while low-fat [odds ratio (OR): 0.19, 95% confidence intervals (CI): 0.05－0.66] and total dairy intake (OR: 0.23, 95% CI: 0.06－0.79) were inversely associated with PCa risk.

confidence_interval.excerpt: High intake of total digestion-resistant BPs, low molecular weight peptides, high molecular weight peptides, phosphorylated residues, disulfide bonds, and antioxidant peptides was not significantly associated with the risk of PCa in the adjusted models (P>0.05), while low-fat [odds ratio (OR): 0.19, 95% confidence intervals (CI): 0.05－0.66] and total dairy intake (OR: 0.23, 95% CI: 0.06－0.79) were inversely associated with PCa risk.
